validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED and well-documented, not a phantom. The 'Pipeline II' segment corresponds to the 3 July 2024 Turkmenistan-Iran gas deal under which Iranian companies will build a NEW 125 km gas pipeline plus three compressor stations on Turkmen territory to raise Dauletabad-Sarakhs-Khangiran-corridor deliveries to Iran to 40 bcm/y (tied to a SWAP contract of up to 10 bcm/y Turkmen gas to Iraq via Iran). Corroborated by >=4 independent outlets: AGBI (2024-07), RFE/RL, worldpipelines.com (2024-07-09), world-energy.org, plus Persian coverage (ISNA/SHANA). The sheet's own cited leads (mfa.gov.tm/news/4626 and neftegaz 841732 'Iranian companies to build 125 km pipeline in Turkmenistan') describe exactly this deal. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a gas transmission trunk. DUPLICATE: not a cross-ProjectID duplicate -- 'Pipeline II' is the proposed 2024 addition within the same D-S-K corridor as the operating 2010 'Pipeline I'; distinct from all 7 other roster rows. ATTRIBUTION: FuelSource 'Dauletabad gas field' correct; Owner Turkmengaz + Iran Ministry of Petroleum plausible (Iranian firms build, Turkmengaz owns Turkmen infra). CAVEATS: (1) province recorded 'Khorasan Khorasan Province' is a typo -- Khangiran/Shahid Hasheminejad refinery is in Razavi Khorasan; (2) endpoints Dauletabad(TM)->Khangiran(Iran) describe the delivery corridor, but the physical 125 km new-build is entirely within Turkmenistan per all sources.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC CHALLENGE on Capacity. The cited neftegaz article (SSL-blocked to the verifier) and every independent source I could read give these numbers: new pipe = 125 km + 3 compressor stations; SWAP contract = up to 10 bcm/y (Turkmen gas to Iraq via Iran); TOTAL corridor target = 40 bcm/y; existing Pipeline I ~12.5 bcm/y and the Korpeje-Kordkuy/Chalyouq route ~8 bcm/y. NONE of them states 19.5 bcm/y for this pipeline. 19.5 appears to be a back-calculated increment (40 total minus ~20.5 existing = 19.5), i.e. not a directly sourced capacity for the new line. Flagging so it is not silently passed; recommend either re-sourcing to a stated figure or reframing the field (e.g. the 10 bcm/y swap volume, or the 40 bcm/y corridor target with a note). Length 125 km, by contrast, is high-confidence (>=4 independent sources agree).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'proposed' still correct. Deal signed 3 July 2024 (ProposalYear 2024 confirmed). Newest independent evidence: Times of Central Asia (Sept 2025) reports NO construction progress and that the swap/pipeline deal is at risk as 'collateral damage' from the June 2025 Israel-Iran conflict, with Iran prioritizing repair of war-damaged infrastructure. A Nov 2025 Turkmen cabinet gas-network upgrade approval (pipeline-journal) is generic and does not specifically name this 125 km line, so it is not verified construction-start evidence. No independent source reports construction has begun. Proposal (July 2024) to last evidence (Sept 2025) is under the 2-year dormancy threshold, and there is ongoing (if uncertain) news, so no dormancy downgrade -- keep 'proposed'. Caveat: momentum has stalled; re-check for a shelved signal at the next annual pass if 2026 brings no construction news.
